en.name: Stephen VI
en.summary: The pope who staged the grotesque Cadaver Synod, posthumously trying his predecessor Formosus's exhumed corpse, and was himself strangled after a popular uprising.
en.body: Stephen VI infamously had the corpse of Formosus exhumed, dressed in papal vestments, and propped up for a macabre posthumous trial that declared his papacy and ordinations invalid, before the body was mutilated and thrown into the Tiber. Public revulsion at the spectacle eventually turned Rome against Stephen himself; he was deposed, imprisoned, and strangled within months, one of several popes of this violent era to die at the hands of Roman factions.
